description: Agent Purchases: submit a provider’s stated refund route for failed paid calls (endpoint, process, automatic, contact-us or none, with its window, where the money goes back to and the proof it requires), each step of the route (endpoint, form, email, ticket, chat or dispute, where it happens, what a test of it showed and what the buyer needs to take it), the failed call (reference, amount, when it failed and when the refund is asked for) and the proof the buyer holds. The signed report gives each step as reachable, unreachable, unpublished or untested, and names every block (no route, contact-us alone, a step written down with nowhere to take it, a step tested and failing, a window already closed) and every gap (a step needing an account an agent may not hold, no stated window, credit in place of money, proof the buyer does not hold). What the seller’s refund rules say is wever_refund-rule-check and whether one purchase qualifies under a refund policy is wever_refund-eligibility-check. Verdict no_working_route, route_gaps, route_unverified or route_reachable. POST /api/refund-path-check. Reads only the material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, sharing, configuration change or external write. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-purchases-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-purchases/.

asked_on.description: When the refund is asked for, as a date.

held.description: Proof the buyer holds, such as the transaction reference and the signed receipt.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

destination.description: Where the money goes back to.

proof_required.description: What the provider requires, such as the transaction reference or the signed receipt.

window.description: How long after a failed call a refund can be asked for, such as 14 days.

steps.description: Each step of the route, in order.

auth.description: What the buyer needs to take the step.

location.description: Where the step happens: a URL, an address or a tool name.

reachable.description: What a test of the step showed.

name: wever_refund-path-check
title: Refund path check
